title: Binary search: lower bound
summary: First index with value >= target, or len(values) if none. Half-open [left, right): too small → left = mid + 1, else right = mid. O(log n).
code: # Exclude mid only when its value is too small.
triggers: sorted input + a position, count or insertion point
first index where a yes/no condition flips to yes
O(log n) expected on ordered data
prompts: Log timestamps are stored in ascending order. Count the entries strictly before a given moment.
Release versions are kept sorted. Find where a new version goes so the order holds.
Exam scores are sorted low to high. Find the first position that reaches the pass mark.
invariant: values[:left] < target <= values[right:]; [left, right) is undecided. When it is empty, left is the answer.
mantra: Too small: step past mid. Otherwise keep mid.
pitfalls: right starts at len(values), not len(values) - 1, so 'absent' can return len(values).
Half-open pairs 'while left < right' with 'right = mid'; mixing in <= or mid - 1 reads past the end or skips the answer.
left = mid (no + 1) stops shrinking once right == left + 1.
Comparing with <= yields upper bound: first value > target.
Python ints don't overflow, so (left + right) // 2 is fine; bisect.bisect_left is the built-in.

anchors.name: Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array
anchors.trick: first = lower_bound(t), last = upper_bound(t) - 1; absent if first == n or values[first] != t.

anchors.name: Koko Eating Bananas
anchors.trick: Same loop over speeds [1, max(piles)]; 'values[mid] < target' becomes 'not feasible(mid)'.

anchors.name: Time Based Key-Value Store
anchors.trick: upper_bound on timestamps, then step back one.

mutations.explanation: When every value is below target it returns the last index instead of len(values).
mid can reach len(values) (IndexError), and right = mid can stop shrinking (infinite loop).
Becomes upper bound: skips values equal to target.
No progress when right == left + 1 and values[mid] < target: infinite loop.
Discards mid even when it is the first match.
